module_title: High Courts of India - Basic Understanding
introduction: The High Court is the highest judicial body at the State level. In the Indian single integrated judicial system, the High Court operates below the Supreme Court but above the Subordinate Courts. Provisions regarding High Courts are found in Part VI of the Constitution (Articles 214 to 231).

core_concepts.title: Establishment (Article 214)
core_concepts.description: The Constitution provides that there shall be a High Court for each state. However, the 7th Amendment Act (1956) authorized the Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more states or for two or more states and a union territory.

core_concepts.title: Appointment of Judges
core_concepts.description: Every judge of a High Court is appointed by the President. The President consults the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and the Governor of the state concerned. For appointing other judges, the Chief Justice of that High Court is also consulted.

core_concepts.title: Qualifications
core_concepts.description: To be appointed as a High Court judge, a person must: 1. Be a citizen of India. 2. Have held a judicial office in India for 10 years, OR 3. Have been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years.

core_concepts.title: Tenure and Removal
core_concepts.description: A High Court judge holds office until the age of 62 years. They can be removed from office by the President on the recommendation of the Parliament (the process is exactly the same as the removal of a Supreme Court judge).

important_entities.name: Calcutta High Court
important_entities.significance: Established in 1862, it was the first of the three High Courts (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras) set up under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Just like the Supreme Court, the Constitution has NOT prescribed any minimum age for appointment as a judge of a High Court.
Note the difference: High Court judges are APPOINTED by the President, but they take their OATH before the Governor of the state.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The Supreme Court (bigger entity) has a higher retirement age (65), while the High Court (state entity) has a slightly lower one (62).

exam_strategy_tips: Who can increase the number of judges in a High Court? Answer: The President (Unlike the Supreme Court, where Parliament does it).
Identify the oldest High Court (Calcutta) and the newest ones (Andhra Pradesh and Telangana).
